samples.summary: Vacuous assertion in the "remembered heading level is inert" suite: the plain-text check passes regardless of the behavior
samples.evidence: `test('plain-text serialization is unaffected', () => expect(serializeText({ blocks: [bulletedHeading] })).toContain('Quarterly results'))` is presented as evidence that a `list-item`'s remembered `headingLevel` is inert. But `packages/docs/src/serialize/text.ts` never reads `headingLevel` at all (its `blockToText` switch only special-cases horizontal-rule/page-break/table and otherwise emits `inlinesToText`), so the text always contains the block's text whether or not the level leaks. The assertion cannot fail for the behavior under test — it is fake coverage inside an otherwise-real invariant suite (the markdown/blockStyleId/DOCX siblings do exercise it).

samples.summary: Entry-parity test checks source text with a regex rather than the modules' actual exports, so it can pass while the real defect (Node entry import failure) exists
samples.evidence: `blockHelperExports` `readFileSync`s `src/index.ts` / `src/node.ts` and scans `/export\s*\{([^}]*)\}\s*from\s*'([^']+)'/g`, filtering on the literal path `'./store/block-helpers.js'`. It therefore only proves the two files contain matching text clauses: a helper re-exported through a different path/alias module, with double quotes, or via `export *` is invisible, and the test never imports either entry to confirm the symbol actually resolves under Node — which is the failure the header comment says it guards. Meaningful but weaker than advertised; an `await import('../../src/node.js')` and comparison of `Object.keys` would test the behavior.

verdict.reason: sanitizeImageData is real and reachable on every internal-flavour paste (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:110-128, called at :160-161 from sanitizeInlineStyle, reached via deserializeBlocks :22-30 and deserializeClipboard :347-360). verdict.reason: The finding is accurate. `sanitizeTableData` (clipboard.ts:255-274) plus the span handling in `sanitizeCell` (:238-241) and the `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH` cap (:59, :256) have no test covering their success path. The tableCells round trip at clipboard.test.ts:89-120 and the validation test at :249-258 go through sanitizeCellRows/sanitizeCell with paragraph-only cells and no colSpan/rowSpan, so they never enter sanitizeTableData, never exercise columnWidths defaulting to 100, rowHeights, or the depth cap. I searched wide for a counterexample: only three files import the clipboard module (grep "view/clipboard") — clipboard.test.ts, test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts (real paste events via serializeClipboard/WAFFLEDOCS_MIME at :10,:461-472, but every payload is paragraphs/headings/bulleted-headings, :88-117, :474-595), and test/model/table-merge-normalize.test.ts (:4, imports only cloneTableCells, which bypasses the sanitizer). grep "version: 1" across all *.test.ts finds hand-built payloads only in clipboard.test.ts, none with tableData. grep colSpan|rowSpan in packages/docs/test hits 11 files, none of which touch the clipboard sanitizer. grep WAFFLEDOCS_MIME/x-waffledocs repo-wide finds no other test; there is no e2e directory. finding.summary: No test that a real `table` block survives the new clipboard sanitizer — only the negative "dropped" case is covered
finding.evidence: The change replaces `payload.blocks as Block[]` with a full rebuild, so every copied `table` block must now pass `sanitizeTableData` (clipboard.ts:255-274), which rebuilds `rows/columnWidths/rowHeights` and returns `undefined` on any shape mismatch — in which case `sanitizeBlock` returns null and the block is silently DROPPED from the paste (clipboard.ts:292-297). `text-editor.ts:1092` copies selected blocks (tables included) through `serializeClipboard`. The only new table assertion is the negative one: `deserializeBlocks(JSON.stringify({version:1, blocks:[{type:'table'}]}))).toEqual([])` (clipboard.test.ts:246). Nothing round-trips a serialized table block and asserts rows/cell text/columnWidths survive, so a sanitizer that drops or mangles every pasted table would keep the suite green. Searched: `deserializeBlocks|deserializeClipboard|WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` across packages/docs/test (only clipboard.test.ts and list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts, neither serializes a table block), plus test/model/paste-table-into-cell.test.ts and test/model/nested-table.test.ts do not touch the clipboard JSON path.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: the JSON clipboard sanitizer's positive table-block path is untested. `sanitizeTableData` (clipboard.ts:255-274) returns undefined on any unusable shape, and `sanitizeBlock` then returns null so the table is silently dropped (clipboard.ts:292-297, 326-331). Copied table blocks genuinely reach this path (text-editor.ts:1091-1093 serialize, 1240-1242 deserialize). The only table assertion against the sanitizer is the negative one at clipboard.test.ts:246 (`{type:'table'}` -> []). The tableCells round-trip at clipboard.test.ts:89-120 exercises sanitizeCellRows/sanitizeCell, not sanitizeTableData; the HTML/markdown table tests (clipboard.test.ts:408-689) bypass the JSON sanitizer entirely. I searched repo-wide (all non-.md files) for deserializeBlocks|deserializeClipboard|serializeClipboard|WAFFLEDOCS_MIME|x-waffledocs: only clipboard.test.ts, list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts, and table-merge-normalize.test.ts (cloneTableCells only) import the module. list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:454-472 does drive a real paste through WAFFLEDOCS_MIME, but a case-insensitive grep for "table" in that file returns zero matches — it pastes only paragraphs/headings. No e2e/integration dirs exist, and no test builds a version:1 payload containing tableData. Decisive: replacing sanitizeTableData's body with `return undefined` would keep the entire suite green, so a sanitizer that drops or mangles every pasted table is undetected — a clear "changed behavior with no meaningful test" gap in this lens's lane.

verdict.reason: sanitizeImageData (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:110-128) is the sole survival path for inline images in an internal-clipboard payload: it is called only from sanitizeInlineStyle (clipboard.ts:160), which is reached from sanitizeInlines -> sanitizeBlock -> sanitizeBlocks, used by both deserializeBlocks (clipboard.ts:22-30) and deserializeClipboard (clipboard.ts:347-360). I enumerated every importer of src/view/clipboard.js in the repo: only packages/docs/test/view/clipboard.test.ts, packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts (real paste events via serializeClipboard + WAFFLEDOCS_MIME, lines 454-595) and packages/docs/test/model/table-merge-normalize.test.ts (cloneTableCells only). None of the three constructs an inline with style.image: grep for image/￼ in list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts and table-merge-normalize.test.ts yields zero hits, its paste fixtures are makeHeading/makeParagraph/makeBulletedHeading (lines 88-117), and the new 'clipboard payload validation' block (clipboard.test.ts:177-259) exercises headingLevel, unknown types, junk keys, listLevel clamping, broken payloads and tableCells but never an image. Tests that do build style.image fixtures (test/serialize/text.test.ts:197, test/serialize/markdown.test.ts:331, test/export/docx-exporter.test.ts:289, test/store/block-helpers.test.ts:285, test/view/table-renderer.test.ts:276) drive serializers/exporters/renderers, not clipboard deserialization.
